name: DEADZONE ATLAS: Shelf Survival Open World
description: DEADZONE ATLAS is a full BCI-integrated open-world survival game set in a procedurally generated megacity that is an uncomfortably accurate simulation of GLMZ's Shelf districts — collapsed infrastructure, contested resource nodes, predatory NPC factions modeled on actual corponation security doctrine, and a hunger-fatigue-injury system that players frequently describe as 'too real to be fun.' The game was developed by a two-person team operating out of a Tier 2 apartment using leaked corporate world-building data, and its accuracy to actual Shelf conditions was so precise that HelixCorp's legal division spent eight months trying to determine how the developers obtained their environmental data.
story_hooks: The game's procedural generation engine has begun producing layouts that match real Shelf infrastructure changes before those changes are made public — as if someone with access to HelixCorp planning documents is feeding data to the algorithm.

A Tier 4 urban planning consultant has become obsessed with DEADZONE ATLAS, using it to model humanitarian intervention scenarios in real Shelf districts — but someone in her company wants those models destroyed.
The game's two developers have disappeared; their last known communication was a cryptic update note reading 'we found the source.'
